diagnosisScope: Architecture-level diagnosis only. No professional-reference payload was reopened, no scorer was called, no candidate was modified, and no exact professional-reference note alignment/timing/pitch was derived or reused.

timebaseCodeFacts.contractFeatureTransform: robust-z with median/MAD*1.4826, standard-deviation fallback, no positive clipping
timebaseCodeFacts.gridMapping: each detected beat is mapped into a four-sixteenth-step beat ordinal derived from Viterbi state deltas

findings.title: Pathological beat density makes the musical coordinate system unusable
evidence: The frozen structural QC reports 2,986 tracked beats.
The sole generation run reports approximately 216.45 seconds of separated audio.
Those facts imply approximately 827.72 tracked beats per minute and one tracked beat every 72.49 ms.
The grid contract assigns four sixteenth steps to each tracked beat, so this density compresses musical grid cells to a physically implausible scale.

Both Guitar and Bass have near-zero timing-aware and same-measure pitch matches even though generated event counts are not orders of magnitude away from the frozen score counts. A shared coordinate-system failure is therefore the dominant cross-stream explanation.
findings.conclusion: The V158 timebase is catastrophically invalid before Guitar/Bass recognizer quality can be meaningfully judged.

findings.title: Signed robust-z onset envelope is unsafe as direct beat-tracker input
evidence: The sealed numeric contract explicitly specifies robust-z feature transforms with no positive clipping.
The implementation directly averages robust-z mix and drum onset-strength arrays and passes the signed result to librosa.beat.beat_track.
The sole generation run emitted 'RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in log1p' from librosa rhythm processing during timebase construction.
The resulting beat count is pathological by direct duration arithmetic.
findings.conclusion: A signed/invalid fused beat envelope is the strongest architecture-level cause currently supported without reopening the professional reference. It must be eliminated in the next architecture rather than tuned against V158 score details.

findings.title: Bar-phase inference is incorrectly coupled to absolute beat ordinal
evidence: The implementation converts Viterbi state transitions into the absolute beat ordinal instead of using state inference only to label downbeat/bar phase.
Same-state transitions add zero beats and skip-one transitions add two beats, so a bar-phase model can stretch or compress the absolute time coordinate.
The frozen state population is strongly nonuniform, with state 3 appearing only 413 times versus 924 state-0 labels.
findings.conclusion: Future timebase architecture should derive absolute beat ordinal monotonically from beat index and use bar-state inference only for phase/bar boundaries.

findings.title: Guitar proposal fusion is over-complete but cannot be responsibly retuned from V158
evidence: V158 generated 1,701 combined-Guitar events versus 1,393 in the already-frozen aggregate score, an excess of 308 events (approximately 22.1%).
370 generated Guitar events came from harmonic_track additions on top of 1,331 Basic Pitch events.
The aggregate score does not provide source-conditional accuracy, so assigning blame to one source or choosing a threshold from this score would be unsupported and reference-guided.
findings.conclusion: Fix and validate the timebase first. Any later Guitar-source redesign must be preregistered generically and evaluated on a fresh independently generated version, never by filtering V158.

findings.title: Bass event count is comparatively close but pitch/time attribution remains unresolved
evidence: V158 generated 465 Bass events versus 547 in the already-frozen aggregate score, a deficit of 82 events (approximately 15.0%).
Only 13 events matched the measure/pitch diagnostic and only one matched the primary timing-aware pitch criterion.
Because the same pathological timebase affects Bass and Guitar, V158 cannot isolate whether Bass pitch fusion itself is the main remaining error after timebase repair.
findings.conclusion: Do not tune pYIN/harmonic-fusion constants from V158. Re-evaluate Bass only after a fresh version has a structurally sane reference-blind timebase.

futureArchitectureRequirements.requirement: Beat-tracker input must be finite and nonnegative by construction; signed robust-z features may be used for bar/downbeat evidence but not as the direct beat-strength envelope.
Absolute beat ordinal must advance exactly once per accepted beat. Bar/downbeat-state inference must not add, delete, duplicate, stretch, or compress beat ordinal.

Reference-blind structural QC must reject pathological beat density before candidate freeze using only audio duration, detected beat times, and tracker-internal tempo evidence; it must not use professional-reference timing.

Reference-blind QC must record audio duration, beat count, mean/median inter-beat interval, implied beat-rate BPM, tracker-reported tempo, beat-rate/tempo consistency, state transition counts, and resulting grid extent.
Any NaN/Inf or runtime warning attributable to beat/rhythm construction must fail timebase QC before a candidate can become authoritative.
Do not sweep or retune Guitar/Bass pitch thresholds from V158 aggregate score. Preserve a single preregistered configuration for the next independently generated candidate.

prohibitedReuse: No V158 candidate modification or filtering.
No professional-reference payload reopen for V158 diagnosis.
No exact reference-derived shift, tempo, pitch histogram, note timing, event location, or correction constant.
No source-specific threshold tuning inferred from the V158 score.
No GPU/Modal/CUDA execution without fresh explicit user authorization.

sequence: Preregister a timebase-first architecture that satisfies REQ-TIMEBASE-1 through REQ-TIMEBASE-5 before implementation code is written.
Implement and independently structurally QC the timebase before permitting Guitar/Bass candidate emission.
Generate exactly one fresh reference-blind CPU candidate only after the timebase QC contract is sealed.
Score that candidate at most once under its own one-shot frozen-reference protocol.
Do not proceed to role/string/fret/technique/PDF stages unless both frozen front-end gates pass.
